questions.question: A model shows high training accuracy but low validation accuracy. What is the best first diagnostic step?

options.A: Check for overfitting by comparing training vs validation curves
options.B: Delete the validation set
options.C: Increase the learning rate to maximum
options.D: Add more layers immediately

questions.explanation: Comparing training and validation performance curves helps confirm overfitting before choosing a remedy.

questions.question: Which SageMaker deployment option is best for a workload with unpredictable, bursty traffic and cold-start tolerance?

options.A: Serverless Inference
options.B: A single fixed always-on large instance
options.C: Batch transform only
options.D: On-premises deployment

questions.explanation: Serverless Inference scales automatically with traffic and is cost-effective for unpredictable, intermittent workloads.

questions.question: What does 'precision' measure in a classification model?

options.A: The proportion of positive predictions that were actually correct
options.B: The proportion of actual positives correctly identified
options.C: The total number of predictions made
options.D: The average training time

questions.explanation: Precision is true positives divided by all predicted positives, measuring how many flagged items were truly positive.

questions.question: What does 'recall' measure in a classification model?

options.A: The proportion of actual positives that were correctly identified
options.B: The proportion of predictions that were positive
options.C: The model's total inference time
options.D: The number of features used

questions.explanation: Recall is true positives divided by all actual positives, measuring how many real positives the model caught.

questions.question: A retailer wants to group customers into unknown segments based on purchasing behavior. Which technique fits best?

options.A: K-means clustering
options.B: Linear regression
options.C: Supervised classification with existing labels
options.D: Reinforcement learning

questions.explanation: K-means clustering is an unsupervised technique well suited to discovering natural groupings without predefined labels.

questions.question: What is the effect of setting a very high learning rate during training?

options.A: Training may become unstable or fail to converge
options.B: Training will always converge faster and more accurately
options.C: It has no effect on convergence
options.D: It eliminates the need for a loss function

questions.explanation: An excessively high learning rate can cause the optimizer to overshoot minima, leading to unstable or divergent training.

questions.question: What is the effect of setting a very low learning rate during training?

options.A: Training converges slowly and may get stuck before reaching an optimal solution
options.B: Training always converges instantly
options.C: It guarantees the best possible model
options.D: It has no effect on training time

questions.explanation: A very low learning rate makes small parameter updates, slowing convergence and potentially getting stuck in suboptimal regions.

questions.question: Which SageMaker built-in algorithm is commonly used for tabular data classification/regression with strong out-of-box performance?

options.A: XGBoost
options.B: Object2Vec only
options.C: Seq2Seq only
options.D: Random Cut Forest only

questions.explanation: XGBoost is a widely used, high-performing gradient boosting algorithm well suited to structured/tabular data tasks.

questions.question: What is Amazon SageMaker Random Cut Forest primarily used for?

options.A: Anomaly detection
options.B: Text summarization
options.C: Image classification
options.D: Speech synthesis

questions.explanation: Random Cut Forest is a SageMaker built-in algorithm designed for unsupervised anomaly detection.

questions.question: A company's model performs well overall but poorly for a specific demographic subgroup. What SageMaker capability helps identify this?

options.A: SageMaker Clarify's bias metrics broken down by subgroup
options.B: SageMaker Ground Truth labeling
options.C: SageMaker Neo compilation
options.D: SageMaker Debugger's profiling report only

questions.explanation: SageMaker Clarify can compute bias and performance metrics across specified subgroups to reveal disparities.

questions.question: What is the purpose of SageMaker Debugger?

options.A: To monitor and debug training jobs in real time, capturing metrics like vanishing gradients
options.B: To label training data
options.C: To deploy models to production
options.D: To manage billing alerts

questions.explanation: SageMaker Debugger provides real-time insight into training jobs, helping detect issues like exploding or vanishing gradients.

questions.question: Which evaluation metric is most appropriate for a regression task predicting continuous house prices?

options.A: Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE)
options.B: F1 score
options.C: Accuracy
options.D: AUC-ROC

questions.explanation: RMSE is a standard regression metric measuring average prediction error magnitude in the same units as the target.

questions.question: What does 'stratified sampling' help achieve when splitting a dataset for an imbalanced classification problem?

options.A: Ensures each split maintains the same class proportions as the overall dataset
options.B: Removes the minority class entirely
options.C: Increases dataset size artificially
options.D: Guarantees 100% model accuracy

questions.explanation: Stratified sampling preserves class distribution across training/validation/test splits, important for imbalanced data.

questions.question: Which SageMaker capability would help compress and optimize a trained model for deployment on edge devices?

options.A: SageMaker Neo
options.B: SageMaker Ground Truth
options.C: SageMaker Data Wrangler
options.D: SageMaker Feature Store

questions.explanation: SageMaker Neo compiles and optimizes models to run efficiently on specific target hardware, including edge devices.

questions.question: A company needs to run inference on large datasets stored in S3 without needing an always-on endpoint. Which SageMaker inference option fits best?

options.A: Batch Transform
options.B: Real-time endpoint with auto-scaling
options.C: Serverless Inference with 1-second timeout
options.D: SageMaker Studio notebooks only

questions.explanation: Batch Transform processes large datasets asynchronously without requiring a persistent hosted endpoint.

questions.question: What is a key reason to use k-fold cross-validation over a single train/test split for a small dataset?

options.A: It gives a more reliable performance estimate by testing on multiple different data splits
options.B: It eliminates the need for any test data
options.C: It always increases model accuracy
options.D: It reduces the dataset size needed

questions.explanation: K-fold cross-validation averages results across multiple splits, providing a more robust performance estimate, especially valuable with limited data.

questions.question: Which technique would most directly help address class imbalance during model training?

options.A: Applying class weighting or oversampling the minority class
options.B: Increasing the learning rate
options.C: Reducing the number of features
options.D: Removing the validation set

questions.explanation: Class weighting or oversampling gives the minority class more influence during training, helping address imbalance.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of one-hot encoding a categorical feature?

options.A: To convert categorical values into a numeric format that ML algorithms can process without implying ordinal relationships
options.B: To compress the dataset size
options.C: To remove missing values
options.D: To normalize numeric features

questions.explanation: One-hot encoding represents categories as binary vectors, avoiding false ordinal relationships that a single numeric code could imply.

questions.question: Why might a data scientist use SageMaker Data Wrangler's bias report before training a model?

options.A: To detect potential bias in the dataset early, before it propagates into the trained model
options.B: To automatically deploy the model
options.C: To reduce storage costs
options.D: To generate synthetic images

questions.explanation: Checking for bias during data preparation helps catch and address fairness issues before they are baked into a trained model.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of using SageMaker Multi-Model Endpoints?

options.A: Hosting multiple models on a single endpoint to reduce cost and simplify management for many low-traffic models
options.B: Guaranteed zero latency for all models
options.C: Automatic model retraining
options.D: Eliminating the need for IAM roles

questions.explanation: Multi-model endpoints let you host many models behind one endpoint, sharing compute resources and reducing per-model hosting cost.

questions.question: Which is a valid reason to use gradient boosting over a single decision tree?

options.A: Gradient boosting combines many weak learners sequentially to improve accuracy and reduce bias
options.B: Gradient boosting always trains faster than a single tree
options.C: A single decision tree always overfits less
options.D: Gradient boosting requires no hyperparameter tuning

questions.explanation: Gradient boosting builds an ensemble of weak learners that sequentially correct prior errors, typically improving accuracy over a single tree.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'elbow method' in unsupervised learning?

options.A: A technique to help choose the optimal number of clusters in k-means clustering
options.B: A method to tune learning rate
options.C: A technique for image cropping
options.D: A method to encrypt data

questions.explanation: The elbow method plots within-cluster variance against cluster count to help identify a good number of clusters (k).

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why feature scaling matters for algorithms like k-nearest neighbors or gradient descent-based models?

options.A: Features with larger numeric ranges can disproportionately dominate distance calculations or gradient updates
options.B: Feature scaling has no effect on distance-based or gradient-based algorithms
options.C: Scaling always reduces dataset size
options.D: Scaling is only relevant for image data

questions.explanation: Unscaled features with large ranges can dominate distance metrics or gradient magnitudes, skewing model behavior.

questions.question: What is a practical benefit of SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning using Bayesian optimization over grid search?

options.A: It more efficiently explores the hyperparameter space by learning from previous trial results
options.B: It guarantees the global optimum every time
options.C: It requires no compute resources
options.D: It eliminates the need for a validation metric

questions.explanation: Bayesian optimization uses prior trial results to intelligently choose the next hyperparameters to try, often more efficient than exhaustive grid search.

questions.question: Which scenario best justifies choosing a decision tree model over a neural network?

options.A: When interpretability of individual predictions is a priority and the dataset is tabular and moderately sized
options.B: When the task requires processing raw images at scale
options.C: When maximum possible accuracy on massive unstructured datasets is the only priority
options.D: When the model must generate free-form text

questions.explanation: Decision trees offer clear, interpretable decision paths, making them attractive for tabular problems where explainability matters.

questions.question: What is 'early stopping' in neural network training?

options.A: Halting training when validation performance stops improving, to prevent overfitting
options.B: Stopping training immediately after one epoch always
options.C: A method to increase training data size
options.D: A hardware failure recovery mechanism

questions.explanation: Early stopping monitors validation performance and halts training once it plateaus or worsens, helping prevent overfitting.

questions.question: Why would a team use SageMaker Pipelines instead of manually running each ML step?

options.A: To create a repeatable, auditable, and automated workflow across data prep, training, and deployment
options.B: To eliminate all need for compute resources
options.C: To bypass IAM permissions
options.D: To avoid using S3 for storage

questions.explanation: Pipelines automate and standardize the ML workflow, improving repeatability, auditability, and operational efficiency.

questions.question: Which factor most directly determines whether a supervised or unsupervised approach is appropriate for a given problem?

options.A: Whether labeled data with known correct outputs is available
options.B: The size of the AWS account
options.C: The programming language used
options.D: The number of AWS regions used

questions.explanation: The availability of labeled data is the key deciding factor between supervised and unsupervised learning approaches.

questions.question: What does a high variance, low bias model typically indicate?

options.A: The model likely overfits, performing well on training data but poorly on new data
options.B: The model is too simple to capture patterns
options.C: The model has zero prediction error always
options.D: The model cannot be evaluated

questions.explanation: High variance/low bias suggests the model closely fits training data (including noise), often generalizing poorly.

questions.question: Which SageMaker feature is designed to help detect concept drift in a deployed model over time?

options.A: SageMaker Model Monitor
options.B: SageMaker Ground Truth
options.C: SageMaker Canvas
options.D: SageMaker JumpStart

questions.explanation: Model Monitor continuously checks incoming data and predictions against a baseline to detect drift after deployment.

questions.question: What is a reasonable next step if a model shows both high bias and high variance (poor performance everywhere and inconsistent results)?

options.A: Reassess data quality, feature engineering, and model architecture from the ground up
options.B: Simply retrain with the exact same setup repeatedly
options.C: Ignore the issue since it will resolve itself
options.D: Immediately deploy to production regardless

questions.explanation: Poor performance combined with instability often signals deeper issues in data quality or model design requiring holistic review.

questions.question: Which of these best describes the purpose of a 'weighted loss function' for imbalanced classification?

options.A: Assigning higher penalty to misclassifying the minority class to counteract class imbalance during training
options.B: Reducing the overall dataset size
options.C: Increasing training speed only
options.D: Removing the need for evaluation metrics

questions.explanation: Weighted loss functions penalize minority-class errors more heavily, helping the model pay proper attention to underrepresented classes.

questions.question: A team is deciding between SageMaker Autopilot and manually building a custom model. When is Autopilot most appropriate?

options.A: When the team wants a fast, automated baseline with minimal ML expertise required
options.B: When maximum custom control over every architecture decision is required
options.C: When the dataset is unlabeled and unsupervised methods are required
options.D: When deploying to on-premises hardware exclusively

questions.explanation: Autopilot automates model building and is ideal for quickly establishing a solid baseline without deep ML expertise.

questions.question: What is the risk of using accuracy as the sole metric to compare two models on an imbalanced dataset?

options.A: A model that always predicts the majority class could appear to perform well despite being useless for the minority class
options.B: Accuracy is always the most informative metric regardless of class balance
options.C: There is no risk since accuracy is class-agnostic
options.D: Accuracy cannot be computed for imbalanced data

questions.explanation: On imbalanced data, high accuracy can mask a complete failure to correctly identify the minority class.

questions.question: Which of these is an appropriate use of SageMaker Ground Truth Plus?

options.A: Outsourcing high-quality data labeling to an expert workforce managed by AWS
options.B: Automatically deploying a trained model
options.C: Compressing model artifacts
options.D: Managing billing alerts

questions.explanation: Ground Truth Plus provides a fully managed data labeling service using an AWS-managed expert workforce.

questions.question: What is the benefit of using ensemble methods like Random Forest over a single decision tree?

options.A: Combining multiple trees reduces variance and typically improves generalization
options.B: A single tree always generalizes better
options.C: Ensembles eliminate the need for any training data
options.D: Ensembles always run faster than a single tree

questions.explanation: Random Forest averages predictions across many decorrelated trees, reducing variance compared to any single tree.

questions.question: Which scenario is best suited to a time-series forecasting approach rather than standard regression?

options.A: Predicting next month's product demand based on historical sales trends and seasonality
options.B: Classifying whether an email is spam
options.C: Clustering customers into segments
options.D: Detecting objects in an image

questions.explanation: Time-series forecasting explicitly models temporal patterns like trend and seasonality, which standard regression does not inherently capture.

questions.question: What does 'multicollinearity' refer to in the context of regression modeling?

options.A: When two or more input features are highly correlated with each other, making individual effects hard to isolate
options.B: When a model has too few features
options.C: A type of neural network layer
options.D: A method for feature scaling

questions.explanation: Multicollinearity occurs when predictor variables are highly correlated, complicating interpretation of individual feature effects.

questions.question: Why might a data scientist choose to use SageMaker's built-in Linear Learner algorithm?

options.A: For efficient, scalable linear regression or classification on large datasets with built-in regularization options
options.B: For generating images from text
options.C: For processing audio exclusively
options.D: For anomaly detection exclusively

questions.explanation: Linear Learner is a SageMaker built-in algorithm optimized for scalable linear models, supporting both regression and classification.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a held-out test set that is used only once, at the very end of model development?

options.A: To provide an unbiased final estimate of model performance, avoiding overfitting to validation data through repeated tuning
options.B: To train the final production model
options.C: To label new data
options.D: To reduce storage costs

questions.explanation: A truly held-out test set used only at the end avoids the risk of indirectly overfitting to validation data through repeated tuning decisions.

questions.question: Which of these best describes why SageMaker supports 'bring your own container' (BYOC)?

options.A: To let teams run custom training/inference code and dependencies not covered by built-in algorithms
options.B: To eliminate the need for any AWS account
options.C: To automatically label data
options.D: To bypass IAM security entirely

questions.explanation: BYOC allows teams to package custom code, frameworks, and dependencies as containers for training or inference on SageMaker.

questions.question: What is a common reason a model's performance degrades after deployment even without any code changes?

options.A: Data drift, where the real-world input distribution shifts from the training data distribution
options.B: The model's code spontaneously changes
options.C: AWS automatically retrains models without notice
options.D: Deployed models cannot degrade over time

questions.explanation: Real-world data often shifts over time, causing a static model's performance to degrade even without any code changes.

questions.question: Which combination of SageMaker tools would best support a full responsible-ML workflow: bias detection, explainability, and monitoring?

options.A: SageMaker Clarify (bias/explainability) plus SageMaker Model Monitor (ongoing monitoring)
options.B: SageMaker Polly plus SageMaker Kendra
options.C: SageMaker Snowball plus SageMaker Route 53
options.D: SageMaker CloudFront plus SageMaker SES

questions.explanation: Clarify addresses bias detection and explainability, while Model Monitor tracks ongoing data/model quality after deployment.

questions.question: What is a key limitation of relying solely on SHAP or similar feature attribution methods for model explainability?

options.A: They explain individual predictions based on the current model but don't guarantee the model's overall reasoning is sound or fair
options.B: They make models 100% interpretable with no caveats
options.C: They eliminate the need for bias testing
options.D: They cannot be used with any tree-based models

questions.explanation: Feature attribution methods show which inputs influenced a prediction but don't inherently validate that the model's broader logic is correct or unbiased.

questions.question: Why is it important to retrain or update a deployed model periodically?

options.A: To account for data drift and maintain accuracy as real-world patterns evolve
options.B: Deployed models never need updates once trained
options.C: Retraining is only needed if the model was originally wrong
options.D: Retraining eliminates the need for monitoring

questions.explanation: Periodic retraining helps the model stay aligned with evolving real-world data patterns, countering drift-related performance loss.

questions.question: What is the tradeoff of using a very deep neural network with many layers on a small dataset?

options.A: Higher risk of overfitting due to the model's capacity exceeding what the limited data can support
options.B: Guaranteed better performance regardless of data size
options.C: No risk, since more layers always help
options.D: Reduced training time in all cases

questions.explanation: Deep models have high capacity and can overfit small datasets by memorizing rather than generalizing.

questions.question: Which technique helps a model generalize better by penalizing large weight values during training?

options.A: L2 regularization (weight decay)
options.B: Increasing batch size only
options.C: Removing the validation set
options.D: Reducing the number of training examples

questions.explanation: L2 regularization adds a penalty proportional to weight magnitude, discouraging overly complex models and improving generalization.

questions.question: What is a good reason to use SageMaker Studio's experiment tracking capabilities?

options.A: To systematically compare multiple training runs, hyperparameters, and metrics for reproducibility
options.B: To automatically deploy every model version to production
options.C: To eliminate the need for a training dataset
options.D: To bypass IAM permissions

questions.explanation: Experiment tracking helps teams organize, compare, and reproduce results across many training runs and configurations.

questions.question: Which of these is a valid concern when using synthetic data generated to augment a small real-world training dataset?

options.A: Synthetic data may not fully capture the complexity and edge cases of real-world data, risking a model that underperforms in production
options.B: Synthetic data always perfectly represents reality
options.C: Synthetic data eliminates all bias
options.D: Synthetic data cannot be used with any ML algorithm

questions.explanation: Synthetic data can be a useful supplement, but it may miss real-world nuances, so validation against real data remains important.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a champion/challenger deployment strategy for ML models?

options.A: Running a new candidate model alongside the current production model to compare performance before fully replacing it
options.B: Deleting the old model immediately upon deployment
options.C: Running two unrelated models with no comparison
options.D: A billing strategy for AWS resources

questions.explanation: Champion/challenger testing lets teams validate a new model's performance against the current production model before a full rollout.

questions.question: Why might a team prefer a simpler, more interpretable model (like logistic regression) over a complex black-box model in a regulated industry?

options.A: Regulatory requirements often demand explainable decisions, which simpler models can more readily provide
options.B: Simpler models always have higher accuracy
options.C: Complex models are always illegal to use
options.D: Interpretability has no relevance to regulation

questions.explanation: Regulated industries (e.g., finance, healthcare) often require explainable decision-making, favoring inherently interpretable models.

questions.question: What is the purpose of using a learning rate schedule (e.g., decay) during training?

options.A: Gradually reducing the learning rate over time to help the model converge more precisely
options.B: Keeping the learning rate constant is always optimal
options.C: Increasing the learning rate indefinitely improves convergence
options.D: Learning rate schedules eliminate the need for a loss function

questions.explanation: Learning rate schedules reduce step size over training, helping fine-tune convergence toward a good minimum.

questions.question: Which SageMaker feature would help a team collaborate on shared feature definitions across multiple ML projects?

options.A: SageMaker Feature Store
options.B: SageMaker Neo
options.C: SageMaker Debugger
options.D: SageMaker Ground Truth

questions.explanation: Feature Store provides a centralized, shareable repository for engineered features used across teams and models.

questions.question: What does 'F1 score' represent?

options.A: The harmonic mean of precision and recall
options.B: The average of accuracy and loss
options.C: The total number of true negatives
options.D: The training time in seconds

questions.explanation: F1 score balances precision and recall into a single metric, useful when both false positives and false negatives matter.

questions.question: Why would a company choose SageMaker Canvas over building a custom model with code?

options.A: To let business analysts without coding skills build ML models through a visual, no-code interface
options.B: To achieve the absolute highest possible model accuracy in all cases
options.C: To bypass the need for any data
options.D: To eliminate all model evaluation steps

questions.explanation: Canvas is designed for non-technical users to build and use ML models without writing code.

questions.question: What is a practical benefit of using managed spot training for a long-running, non-time-critical training job?

options.A: Significant cost savings by using spare EC2 capacity, with SageMaker handling interruptions via checkpointing
options.B: Guaranteed instant completion
options.C: Elimination of the need for IAM roles
options.D: Automatic model deployment

questions.explanation: Spot training reduces costs substantially for jobs that can tolerate interruptions, since SageMaker manages checkpoint/resume.

questions.question: Which statement about supervised fine-tuning versus training from scratch is most accurate for most business use cases?

options.A: Fine-tuning a pre-trained model is usually faster and requires less data than training from scratch
options.B: Training from scratch is always faster
options.C: Fine-tuning requires more data than training from scratch
options.D: There is no difference in resource requirements

questions.explanation: Fine-tuning leverages existing learned representations, typically requiring far less data and compute than training a new model from scratch.

questions.question: What is a key reason to monitor both data quality and model quality metrics in SageMaker Model Monitor?

options.A: Data issues (e.g., missing values, schema changes) can degrade model performance even without concept drift
options.B: Only model quality metrics matter
options.C: Data quality has no relationship to model performance
options.D: Monitoring is unnecessary if the model passed initial testing

questions.explanation: Both feed-level data quality and model output quality should be monitored, since data pipeline issues can silently degrade performance.

questions.question: Why might a team use a simpler baseline model before investing in a complex deep learning solution?

options.A: To establish whether the added complexity of a deep learning model is actually justified by meaningful performance gains
options.B: Baselines are never useful
options.C: Simple models always outperform complex ones
options.D: To avoid ever evaluating model performance

questions.explanation: A baseline helps quantify whether a more complex approach delivers enough benefit to justify its added cost and complexity.

questions.question: What does it mean if a model has 'high bias'?

options.A: The model is too simple and systematically underfits the underlying patterns in the data
options.B: The model perfectly fits the training data with zero error
options.C: The model is highly sensitive to small changes in training data
options.D: The model requires no further evaluation

questions.explanation: High bias indicates the model's assumptions are too simplistic to capture the true data patterns, leading to underfitting.

questions.question: A team building a customer support chatbot notices it sometimes fabricates policy details not in their documentation. Besides RAG, what additional safeguard would help most?

options.A: Configuring Bedrock Guardrails to restrict topics and adding instructions to only answer from provided context
options.B: Increasing the temperature parameter
options.C: Removing all system instructions
options.D: Disabling logging

questions.explanation: Guardrails plus explicit prompt instructions to stick to provided context reduce the chance of fabricated, out-of-scope answers.

questions.question: Why does increasing the number of tokens in a RAG system's retrieved context not always improve answer quality?

options.A: Irrelevant or excessive context can dilute the signal, increase cost/latency, and sometimes confuse the model
options.B: More context always improves accuracy with no downside
options.C: Token count has no effect on model behavior
options.D: Retrieved context is never relevant to answer quality

questions.explanation: Beyond a point, additional retrieved context can introduce noise and cost without improving, or even hurting, answer relevance.

questions.question: A developer needs consistent, structured JSON output from an LLM for downstream parsing. Which combination of techniques is most effective?

options.A: Explicit format instructions, a few-shot example of the desired JSON structure, and low temperature
options.B: High temperature with no formatting instructions
options.C: No prompt engineering, relying on default behavior
options.D: Only increasing the max token limit

questions.explanation: Clear format instructions, example demonstrations, and lower randomness together improve output structure consistency.

questions.question: What is the primary risk of using a foundation model's default system prompt in a production application without customization?

options.A: The default behavior may not match the specific safety, tone, or scope requirements of the application
options.B: Default prompts always guarantee ideal behavior
options.C: There is no risk since defaults are universally optimized
options.D: Default prompts eliminate the need for guardrails

questions.explanation: Default model behavior is general-purpose and may not enforce the specific constraints or tone needed for a given application.

questions.question: Why might a RAG-based application still produce a hallucinated answer even with relevant documents retrieved?

options.A: The model may not fully ground its response in the retrieved context, blending it with parametric (pre-trained) knowledge
options.B: RAG eliminates all possibility of hallucination
options.C: Retrieved documents are always ignored by the model
options.D: Hallucination only occurs without any retrieval

questions.explanation: Even with RAG, models can still blend retrieved facts with their internal (sometimes incorrect) knowledge, so grounding isn't guaranteed.

questions.question: A company wants to fine-tune a foundation model for a narrow, specialized task with only 500 labeled examples. What is a key risk to consider?

options.A: Overfitting to the small fine-tuning dataset, potentially degrading general capabilities
options.B: There is no risk with fine-tuning regardless of dataset size
options.C: Fine-tuning always requires millions of examples
options.D: Small datasets always improve model generalization

questions.explanation: Fine-tuning on a small dataset risks overfitting and can degrade the model's broader general-purpose capabilities.

questions.question: Which factor most influences the choice between using Amazon Bedrock's on-demand pricing versus Provisioned Throughput?

options.A: Whether the application has sustained, predictable high-volume traffic requiring guaranteed capacity
options.B: The programming language used to call the API
options.C: The number of AWS regions in use
options.D: Whether the model supports image generation

questions.explanation: Provisioned Throughput suits sustained, predictable high-volume needs; on-demand suits variable or lower-volume usage.

questions.question: A prompt engineer notices that adding role-based framing ('You are an expert financial analyst...') improves response quality. What best explains this?

options.A: Role framing helps steer the model's tone, vocabulary, and reasoning style toward the specified persona's expertise
options.B: Role framing has no measurable effect on output
options.C: Role framing always reduces model accuracy
options.D: Role framing bypasses the need for any other prompt content

questions.explanation: Persona/role framing conditions the model to draw on relevant style and knowledge patterns associated with that expert role.

questions.question: What is a key difference between using Bedrock Agents' action groups versus a simple RAG setup?

options.A: Action groups let the model take real actions (e.g., API calls) beyond just retrieving and presenting information
options.B: They are functionally identical
options.C: RAG can execute API calls while action groups cannot
options.D: Action groups only work with image generation models

questions.explanation: RAG focuses on retrieving and grounding information, while agent action groups enable the model to actively perform tasks via APIs.

questions.question: Why is evaluating a fine-tuned model against a held-out test set important, similar to traditional ML?

options.A: To verify the fine-tuned model generalizes well and hasn't overfit to the fine-tuning data
options.B: Evaluation is unnecessary for foundation models
options.C: Fine-tuned models never need evaluation once deployed
options.D: Held-out sets only apply to image models

questions.explanation: Just as with traditional ML, evaluating on unseen data confirms the fine-tuned model generalizes rather than memorizing training examples.

questions.question: A team is deciding between a proprietary model (e.g., Claude via Bedrock) and a self-hosted open-source model for a new application. Which factor most favors the proprietary managed option?

options.A: Reduced operational burden, since AWS manages scaling, availability, and infrastructure
options.B: Proprietary models always cost nothing to use
options.C: Open-source models cannot be used commercially under any circumstances
options.D: Managed models never require any prompt engineering

questions.explanation: Managed foundation models remove the operational overhead of hosting, scaling, and maintaining infrastructure.

questions.question: What does it mean when a foundation model exhibits 'emergent behavior'?

options.A: Capabilities that appear in larger models but were not explicitly present or predictable in smaller versions of similar architecture
options.B: A bug that must always be immediately patched
options.C: A billing anomaly
options.D: A required feature of all foundation models regardless of size

questions.question: Why might using chain-of-thought prompting increase both accuracy and token cost for a reasoning task?

options.B: Chain-of-thought prompting has no effect on token usage
options.C: Chain-of-thought always reduces accuracy
options.D: Chain-of-thought eliminates the need for any output tokens

questions.explanation: Explicit reasoning steps consume additional tokens, trading higher cost/latency for often improved accuracy on complex tasks.

questions.question: A generative AI application must never reveal internal system prompts to end users. Which combination of controls best supports this?

options.A: Guardrails plus prompt design that instructs the model to refuse revealing system instructions, combined with output filtering
options.B: Relying solely on the model's default behavior
options.C: Publishing the system prompt publicly for transparency

questions.explanation: A layered approach combining guardrails, explicit refusal instructions, and output filtering reduces the risk of system prompt leakage.

questions.question: What is the tradeoff of using a larger embedding model for a RAG-based semantic search system?

options.A: Potentially better retrieval quality at the cost of increased compute, storage, and latency for generating and storing embeddings
options.B: No tradeoff exists; larger embedding models are always strictly better with no cost
options.C: Larger embedding models always reduce retrieval quality
options.D: Embedding model size has no effect on system performance

questions.explanation: Larger embedding models can capture richer semantics but require more compute/storage and can increase latency.

questions.question: A company observes inconsistent outputs from their generative AI application for the same input across different requests. Assuming default settings, what is the most likely cause?

options.A: A non-zero temperature setting introducing randomness into token selection
options.B: The model's weights change between requests
options.C: AWS retrains the model between every request
options.D: The context window is disabled

questions.explanation: With temperature above zero, the model samples somewhat randomly among likely tokens, producing varied outputs for identical inputs.

questions.question: Which approach best balances cost and quality when a generative AI application handles both simple FAQs and complex reasoning queries?

options.A: Routing simple queries to a smaller, cheaper model and complex queries to a larger, more capable model
options.B: Always using the largest available model for every query regardless of complexity
options.C: Always using the smallest available model regardless of task difficulty
options.D: Ignoring query complexity entirely

questions.explanation: Model routing based on query complexity optimizes cost by reserving expensive, capable models for tasks that truly need them.

questions.question: What is a key consideration when selecting a vector database for a large-scale, low-latency RAG application?

options.A: Indexing algorithm efficiency, scalability, and query latency at the expected data volume
options.B: Whether the database supports only relational SQL queries
options.C: The color scheme of the database dashboard
options.D: Whether the database can generate images

questions.explanation: Production RAG systems at scale need vector databases optimized for fast approximate nearest neighbor search at high query volumes.

questions.question: Why is it good practice to version-control prompt templates used in a production generative AI application?

options.A: To track changes, enable rollback, and understand how prompt modifications affect output quality over time
options.B: Prompt templates never need version tracking
options.C: Version control only applies to model weights, not prompts
options.D: It eliminates the need for testing prompt changes

questions.explanation: Treating prompts as versioned artifacts supports traceability, rollback, and systematic evaluation of prompt changes over time.

questions.question: A generative AI summarization tool sometimes omits important details present in the source document. What is a likely contributing factor?

options.A: The context window or output length limit may be truncating content, or the prompt may not emphasize completeness
options.B: Summarization tools always capture 100% of source details
options.C: This can only be fixed by using a smaller model
options.D: This issue cannot occur with foundation models

questions.explanation: Truncation from context/output limits, or under-specified prompts, can lead to incomplete summaries missing key details.

questions.question: What is the benefit of using Amazon Bedrock's Model Evaluation with human evaluators rather than automated metrics alone for a creative writing use case?

options.A: Human evaluators can better judge subjective qualities like tone, creativity, and appropriateness that automated metrics may miss
options.B: Human evaluation is always faster than automated metrics

options.D: Human evaluation removes the need for any prompt testing

questions.explanation: Subjective qualities like tone and creativity are often better judged by humans than by automated scoring alone.

questions.question: A financial services company wants to use a foundation model to draft investment summaries but must ensure no direct investment advice is given. Which control is most directly relevant?

options.A: Configuring Bedrock Guardrails with topic restrictions and adding explicit prompt instructions against giving direct advice
options.B: Increasing the max token limit
options.C: Disabling all logging
options.D: Using the largest available model regardless of guardrails

questions.explanation: Topic-restriction guardrails combined with explicit prompt constraints help prevent the model from crossing into prohibited advice.

questions.question: What is a primary reason to chunk documents into smaller segments before generating embeddings for RAG?

options.A: Smaller, focused chunks improve retrieval precision and fit within embedding model input limits
options.B: Chunking always reduces retrieval quality
options.C: Chunking is only relevant for image data
options.D: Chunking eliminates the need for a vector database

questions.explanation: Chunking keeps each embedded unit focused and within model input limits, improving the relevance of retrieved results.

questions.question: Which of these best explains why a well-designed few-shot prompt can outperform a zero-shot prompt on a nuanced classification task?

options.A: Examples demonstrate the exact decision boundary and format expected, reducing ambiguity the model must resolve on its own
options.B: Few-shot prompts always use fewer tokens than zero-shot prompts
options.C: Few-shot prompting disables the model's reasoning ability
options.D: Zero-shot prompts always perform better on all tasks

questions.explanation: Concrete examples clarify subtle distinctions and expected output format, often improving performance on nuanced tasks.

questions.question: A team building an internal coding assistant wants suggestions grounded in their proprietary codebase. What is the most appropriate architecture?

options.A: RAG that retrieves relevant code snippets/documentation from an indexed internal repository to ground suggestions
options.B: Using a public foundation model with no customization or grounding
options.C: Fine-tuning on unrelated public code exclusively
options.D: Disabling the context window entirely

questions.explanation: Grounding suggestions in the actual internal codebase via RAG ensures recommendations are relevant to the company's specific code patterns.

questions.question: What is a key advantage of using Bedrock's unified API across multiple model providers for an application with evolving model needs?

options.A: The application can switch or A/B test different models with minimal code changes
options.B: It guarantees identical behavior across all models with no testing needed

questions.explanation: A unified API simplifies experimenting with and switching between models, though prompts may still need tuning per model.

questions.question: Why might a generative AI application implement a content moderation layer in addition to Bedrock Guardrails?

options.A: To add defense-in-depth and handle edge cases or application-specific policies not covered by generic guardrails
options.B: Guardrails alone always guarantee complete safety with no gaps
options.C: Additional moderation layers are never useful
options.D: Moderation layers replace the need for any prompt engineering

questions.explanation: Layered moderation provides defense-in-depth, catching edge cases and application-specific policy violations generic guardrails might miss.

questions.question: A company's RAG chatbot occasionally answers questions using outdated information despite recent document updates. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: The vector index has not been refreshed/re-ingested since the source documents were updated
options.B: The foundation model automatically updates its own knowledge in real time
options.C: RAG systems cannot use updated documents by design
options.D: The issue is unrelated to the retrieval pipeline

questions.explanation: If the underlying knowledge base/index isn't refreshed after source updates, retrieval will continue returning stale information.

questions.question: What is an appropriate strategy for handling a generative AI model's refusal to answer a legitimate business question due to overly cautious guardrails?

options.A: Review and tune guardrail configurations and prompt instructions to reduce false positives while maintaining necessary safety controls
options.B: Disable all guardrails entirely
options.C: Switch to an unmoderated, unmanaged model with no safety controls
options.D: Ignore the issue since refusals cannot be adjusted

questions.explanation: Guardrail and prompt tuning can reduce over-triggering on legitimate queries while preserving important safety protections.

questions.question: Which best explains why prompt engineering alone may be insufficient for a model to reliably perform a highly specialized domain task (e.g., legal contract analysis)?

options.A: The base model may lack sufficient domain-specific knowledge or patterns that only fine-tuning or strong RAG grounding can address
options.B: Prompt engineering can always fully replace the need for domain data
options.C: Specialized tasks never benefit from fine-tuning or RAG
options.D: Prompt engineering guarantees expert-level performance on any task

questions.explanation: For deeply specialized domains, prompting alone may not compensate for gaps in the base model's domain knowledge; RAG or fine-tuning can help.

questions.question: A team notices their Bedrock-powered application's cost is dominated by long input contexts on every call, even for short user questions. What optimization would most directly reduce cost without hurting relevance?

options.A: Retrieve and include only the most relevant chunks via RAG instead of sending entire documents each time
options.B: Increase the temperature parameter
options.C: Switch to a larger foundation model
options.D: Disable output token limits

questions.explanation: Targeted retrieval of only relevant chunks reduces unnecessary token usage compared to sending full documents on every call.

questions.question: What is the effect of setting temperature to 0 for a foundation model generating structured data extraction output?

options.A: Output becomes maximally deterministic, favoring the highest-probability token at each step, which suits consistent structured tasks
options.B: Output becomes maximally random and creative
options.C: Temperature has no effect when set to 0
options.D: The model stops generating any output

questions.explanation: A temperature of 0 minimizes randomness, producing consistent, deterministic output well suited to tasks needing reliability.

questions.question: Which scenario best justifies using Provisioned Throughput for a custom fine-tuned model on Bedrock?

options.A: A production application with strict, sustained latency and throughput SLAs that on-demand capacity cannot reliably guarantee
options.B: A prototype used only occasionally for testing
options.C: A one-time batch analysis run once a year
options.D: An application with no performance requirements

questions.explanation: Provisioned Throughput reserves dedicated capacity, important for production workloads with strict, sustained performance requirements.

questions.question: A generative AI application must support both English and Spanish users with a single foundation model. What is a key evaluation step before launch?

options.A: Testing model output quality and safety separately in both languages, since performance can vary by language
options.B: Assuming performance in one language guarantees equal performance in another
options.C: Only testing in the developer's native language
options.D: Skipping evaluation since foundation models perform identically across all languages

questions.explanation: Model performance and safety behavior can vary across languages, so each supported language should be independently evaluated.

questions.question: What is a likely reason an LLM-based application incorrectly answers a multi-step arithmetic word problem?

options.A: LLMs can struggle with precise multi-step calculation without techniques like chain-of-thought prompting or external tool use
options.B: LLMs always perform perfect arithmetic natively
options.C: Arithmetic errors only occur with the smallest models
options.D: This type of error is impossible for foundation models

questions.explanation: LLMs generate text token-by-token and can make calculation errors; chain-of-thought prompting or calling an external calculator tool helps.

questions.question: Which factor is most important when deciding whether to fine-tune a model versus using prompt engineering with a larger context for a document classification task?

options.A: Volume and stability of labeled data, expected query volume, and whether prompt-based approaches already meet accuracy needs
options.B: Only the AWS region where the application is hosted

questions.explanation: The decision hinges on practical factors like data availability, scale, and whether simpler prompting approaches already achieve acceptable accuracy.

questions.question: A team's Bedrock Agent occasionally calls the wrong action group for a user's request. What is a likely remediation?

options.A: Improve the clarity and specificity of each action group's description so the model can better distinguish when to use it
options.B: Remove all action group descriptions entirely
options.C: Increase the temperature to maximum
options.D: Disable the agent's reasoning capability

questions.explanation: Agents select actions based partly on their descriptions; clearer, more distinct descriptions reduce action-selection errors.

questions.question: What is the main reason enterprises often prefer RAG over full fine-tuning for keeping a generative AI application's knowledge current?

options.A: RAG avoids the cost, complexity, and delay of retraining while allowing near-real-time updates by refreshing the retrieval index
options.B: Fine-tuning is always cheaper and faster than RAG
options.C: RAG requires no data infrastructure at all
options.D: Fine-tuning automatically stays current without any retraining

questions.explanation: RAG decouples knowledge updates from the model itself, letting teams refresh the index without expensive retraining cycles.

questions.question: A generative AI application generates plausible-looking but incorrect citations. What combination of practices best mitigates this?

options.A: Grounding responses in retrieved sources via RAG and validating that cited sources actually exist and support the claim
options.B: Increasing temperature to introduce more creative citations
options.C: Removing all source-related instructions from the prompt
options.D: Ignoring the issue since citation accuracy cannot be improved

questions.question: Why might a company choose a mixture of foundation models (a smaller model for triage, a larger model for complex cases) in a single application?

options.C: Because a single model can never handle more than one type of query
options.D: Because larger models cannot be used for simple queries

questions.explanation: Tiered model routing balances cost and performance by matching model capability to task complexity.

questions.question: What does 'catastrophic forgetting' refer to in the context of fine-tuning a foundation model?

options.A: The model losing previously learned general capabilities as it is heavily fine-tuned on a narrow new task
options.B: A hardware failure during training
options.C: A billing error during fine-tuning

questions.explanation: Catastrophic forgetting occurs when fine-tuning overwrites broader general knowledge/capabilities the base model previously had.

options.B: Evaluating each prompt version on a different, randomly chosen dataset

questions.question: What is a good reason to periodically re-evaluate a deployed generative AI application even if the underlying foundation model hasn't changed?

questions.question: What is an appropriate way to handle a situation where a foundation model consistently underperforms on a specific, well-defined subtask within a broader application?
